observations: Photo 0: Front view of a black HP laptop on a purple couch. The screen is off, reflecting surroundings. HP logo visible below screen. Keyboard has a textured surface, trackpad below. Intel sticker on bottom right of keyboard. Two other similar laptops visible in background.
Photo 1: Overhead view of three similar HP laptops arranged on the same purple couch. All screens are off. HP logos visible on each. One laptop is slightly tilted, showing its hinge and side profile.

Photo 2: Side view of one laptop being held at an angle, showing the hinge and keyboard. The screen is tilted back, suggesting a 360-degree hinge. Intel sticker visible. Hand holding the laptop, wearing a white smartwatch.

All laptops appear to be identical models, likely 2-in-1 convertibles. The hinge design supports the 'X360' claim. No visible damage to the chassis or screen in the photos. No model number or serial visible on any surface.

No internal components are visible. The claim about storage capacity and upgradeability cannot be verified remotely.
RAM is internal and not visible. Cannot be confirmed from photos.
Photo 2 shows the laptop being held with the screen folded back, indicating a 360-degree hinge, consistent with 'X360' design.

risks.risk: The laptop may not be a ProBook 11 G9 as claimed; it could be a different model (e.g., HP 11 G9 or another series).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label on the bottom of the laptop or the BIOS screen showing the exact model name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic HP 2-in-1 convertible, not as a ProBook 11 G9, which may be worth less.

risks.risk: The processor may not be 12th generation Intel; it could be an older or lower-tier model.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information or BIOS showing the exact CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has an unspecified Intel processor, which reduces value compared to a confirmed 12th gen chip.

risks.risk: The 128GB SSD and 8GB RAM may not be accurate; the device may have less storage or RAM, or the RAM may not be upgradeable.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information showing storage and RAM details, or a photo of the open laptop showing the RAM slots and SSD.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has unknown storage and RAM, which could be less than claimed, reducing value.

risks.risk: The touchscreen may be non-functional or damaged, which is not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A video clip showing the touchscreen being used to draw or tap, or a photo of the screen with a finger interacting with it.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if the touchscreen is non-functional, which reduces value significantly.
